sections.html:
Layton is Davis County's largest city, on the northern Wasatch Front about 25 miles north of Salt Lake City and 15 miles south of Ogden. The 2020 count was 81,773 residents and the July 2025 estimate is 85,308. Hill Air Force Base sits on the northern edge, Clearfield and South Weber lie beyond it, and Kaysville and Syracuse border the city to the south and west.

The east side climbs toward the foothills and Adams Canyon, the middle follows I-15 where shopping and hotels cluster, and the west side runs flatter toward the lake wetlands. Housing arrived in waves, which means a single street can hold 1960s ramblers with homes from the 1990s and later subdivisions. Condition swings widely from block to block.

Lake effect snow and hot summers wear down roofs and furnaces, and an aging one tends to turn up on a buyer's inspection report. Owners of older houses often choose at that point between fixing things and selling as-is.

sections.h2: Hill Air Force Base and your timeline
sections.html:
Hill Field opened on November 7, 1940 and was renamed Hill Air Force Base on February 5, 1948. Its Ogden Air Logistics Complex provides engineering and logistics management for aircraft such as the F-35, F-16 and A-10, and units on base include the 75th Air Base Wing and the 388th and 419th Fighter Wings. Assignments, deployments and retirements keep local housing turning over.

If a transfer forces you out by a set day, a listing that may sit for weeks is a poor fit. Many cash buyers will close on a date you name.

Retail and hospitality cluster along I-15, including Layton Hills Mall, Restaurant Row, over 1,000 hotel beds and the Davis Conference Center. East Gate Business Park and a Weber State University campus add jobs and students.

I-15 runs through the center of town with exits at Antelope Drive, Hillfield Road and Layton Parkway. US-89 hugs the east edge near the foothills, SR-193 passes the base's south gate, and SR-177 serves the west. FrontRunner stops at Layton Station, built where the old Union Pacific depot stood. Homes near the station or an I-15 ramp suit commuters bound for Salt Lake City or Ogden.

Davis School District serves Layton. Layton High School opened in 1966 and Northridge High School in 1992, and the Northern Utah Academy for Math, Engineering and Science is an early college charter school partnered with Weber State. Buyers often ask which boundary a house falls in, so confirm the address with the district and do not rely on a listing description.

Parks that appeal to buyers include Layton Commons Park, Ellison Park and Legacy Park, plus the Edward A. Kenley Centennial Amphitheater and the Layton Utah Temple, dedicated on June 16, 2024.

Enforcement runs through the police department and centers on how the outside of a property looks. A buyer or lender who notices a violation can stall your sale, and unpaid cleanup bills can follow you.

Layton code ruleRequirement
Weeds and grass12 inches or shorter
Junk, appliances, tires, building materialsStored only inside a structure with walls and a roof
VehiclesRegistered, operable and parked on a hard surface
Expired registration, four months or moreVehicle removed or enclosed
Trees and bushesAt least 7 feet above sidewalks, 13 feet 6 inches above streets

First comes a 14-day courtesy notice. After a re-inspection, a Notice of Ordinance Violation can go to the City Attorney's Office. If an owner never cleans up, a judge can order the city to remove the violations and bill the owner plus an administrative fee.

Owners of vacant or inherited houses who live elsewhere can miss these notices. To learn whether anything is open, email codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov or call (801) 497-8300.

Late July is when Davis County mails the valuation notice, and the appeal period ends in mid-September. Phone Tax Administration for the exact day before you file.

County commissioners double as the Board of Equalization. Market value is the only thing you can contest, and the filer must be the owner or an agent holding notarized authorization. Useful proof: closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales close to January 1, or documented errors in assessor records.

You will find Tax Administration at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, or at 801-451-3331 and taxadmin@daviscountyutah.gov. If you bought recently, your closing statement is strong support.

Your main home gets a 45 percent break on market value, so 55 percent is taxable. To qualify, someone must live there for 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, and each household claims one exemption only.

The break stays with you, not the house. Buyers send Form TC-473A to the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and late forms are refused. Miss it and the same house can be taxed at 100 percent of value for a year, so give your buyer a heads-up.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Layton
sections.html:
The title steps match any other sale, minus the mortgage approval. The seller signs a purchase contract, a title company searches for liens, and the deed is recorded with the Davis County Recorder in Farmington.

  • Share the address, the condition and any deadline, such as a base transfer or a code notice.
  • Review the offer and the closing date the buyer proposes.
  • Sign the contract and let the title company clear liens, unpaid property taxes and any open code charges.
  • Sign the deed at closing and receive the proceeds after payoffs.

Davis County offers a Property Watch email alert that tells an owner when the title on a parcel changes. Sellers who live away from Layton, or who inherited a house, can sign up to hear about any change.

Without a mortgage, you skip the lender's appraisal and any repair list it would demand. There are no open houses, no staging and no weeks of showings. You also pick the closing date, which helps a great deal when a transfer, a deployment or an inheritance sets the clock for you. The title company still checks for liens and prepares the deed.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or open code charges
sections.html: Open property taxes and code charges are paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask Tax Administration and the code enforcement office for current balances, then give both numbers to the title officer so your payout is clear before the signing.

faqs.a: Layton is the largest city in Davis County. The 2020 count was 81,773 residents, with an estimate of 85,308 for July 2025.

faqs.q: Does Hill Air Force Base affect Layton home sales?
faqs.a: Yes, indirectly. The base borders Layton and is one of the largest employers in Utah, so moves and retirements regularly bring owners who need to sell or buy on a set schedule.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property tax valuation notices mailed?
faqs.a: At the end of July each year. Appeals close in mid-September, so confirm the exact date with Tax Administration at 801-451-3331.

faqs.q: Can code enforcement notices be fixed before selling a house in Layton?
faqs.a: Yes. Layton starts with a 14-day courtesy notice, and weeds, junk or an inoperable vehicle can often be cleared in that window. Email codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov to ask what is open on an address.

faqs.q: Does a buyer keep the primary residence exemption on a Layton house?
faqs.a: Not automatically. New owners must file Form TC-473A by September 15 to receive the 45 percent exemption, and a late filing can mean tax on full market value for that year.
